title: Share of the total bird loss concentrated in 12 common families

source.name: Decline of the North American avifauna
source.publisher: Rosenberg et al., Science (Cornell Lab of Ornithology / American Bird Conservancy)

notes: Twelve familiar bird families -- including sparrows, warblers, blackbirds and finches -- accounted for 90% of the net 3-billion-bird loss, meaning the crisis is concentrated in common, everyday backyard species rather than rare ones.
